title: NO KINGS: Reclaiming Our Flag Day
description:
Join us at Wyoming’s State capital in Cheyenne on Saturday June 14th from 12 pm to 2:30 pm as we aim to lift up and take back our wonderful flag.

June 14th is the next big National Day of Action, and some cities are split in their themes, with some choosing to protest the narcissistic birthday of Donald Trump but we choose to take a stand for our flag and other flags that we are fighting for considering June 14 is flag day.

Flag day is getting overshadowed by the ego boosting birthday celebration that is planned but there are more important things to focus on than making it seem like the day is about him. 

So, in defiance of the corruption, abuses of power and everything else that is going on with the Trump administration we will take back our flag and restore it to the prestige it once had.

A little background about flag day, on June 14th, 1777, the Continental congress formally approved the design for the national flag and President Woodrow Wilson officially designated June 14th as national flag day.

The beloved American flag has always been known to have been a symbol of hope, peace, freedom and justice, among other things. But Donald Trump and his cult following have managed to desecrate our flag and turn it into a symbol of hate, bigotry, greed, fear and just overall negativity. In his first presidency and this current one, he has managed to weaponize the flag in a way that is completely opposite of everything the flag stands for.

It’s long overdue we take a stand for our flag and other flags that we are fighting for. Its time to take back our flag and restore it to its meaning and purpose. The American flag needs to be raised up and give people hope again like it did in powerful moments such as when firemen raised the flag at the site of the 9/11 attacks, or when it was famously raised during the battle of Iwo Jima in World War 2.

Our freedom of speech and rights being tampered with won't stop us from proclaiming that Donald Trump is no king! Come show that the flag doesn’t belong to Donald Trump! It belongs to us! So, if you are in or near Cheyenne on June 14th, come make your presence known at the State capital building. Bring family and friends to this positive and peaceful but spirited protest. title: The Roadmap for Winning: A Conversation with Adam Kinzinger and North Texas Local Election Winners
description:
Join us for Roadmap to Winning, a powerful gathering to celebrate how we beat back MAGA extremism—not with more money, but with more heart, more truth, and the will of the people. 

This event is more than a victory lap—it’s a strategy session for the future. We turned the tide in 2025. Now, we build the momentum to turn this first blue wave into a tidal wave in 2026. Learn from the organizers, leaders, and everyday heroes who made it happen—and how we do it again, bigger and bolder.

Together, we map the road ahead. Let’s keep fighting. Let’s keep winning.

**Featured Guest: Adam Kinzinger**

Adam Kinzinger is a former Republican congressman from Illinois and U.S. Air Force veteran known for his outspoken opposition to MAGA extremism. A key member of the January 6th Committee, he prioritized truth and accountability over party loyalty. After leaving Congress, he founded Country First to promote democracy and combat political division.

_**Panelists:**_

**Dr. John Biggan: HEB ISD Trustee**

Dr. John Biggan is a cognitive neuroscientist and data scientist who works in the child welfare system, using research and data to improve the lives of the children in this community, the state, and nationwide. A longtime Hurst resident and advocate for public education, he brings a research-driven approach to his role on the HEB ISD Board of Trustees, focusing on student success, teacher support, and fiscal responsibility.

**Vanessa Pacheco: Richardson ISD Trustee**

Vanessa Pacheco, single-member district 2; elected in June 2022. Mrs. Pacheco is the Chief Operations Officer for Carrolton Injury Law. She and her husband, Jorge, have a daughter who graduated from Berkner High School in 2020 and a son who graduated from Richardson High School in 2023.

**Amir Omar: Richardson Mayor**

Amir Omar is believed to be the first Muslim elected to political office in North Texas. Omar was elected to the Richardson City Council, Place 7 in May 2009, defeating incumbent Dennis Stewart by 51.54% to 48.46%. On May 3, 2025, Omar defeated incumbent Bob Dubey 54.4% to 41.6% in the mayoral race.

**Laney Hawes: Texas Freedom to Read Project and, Keller ISD Families for Public Education; Co-Founder**

Laney Hawes is the Co-Founder of the Texas Freedom to Read Project and the hyper local organization, Keller ISD Families for Public Education.  She's passionate about true grassroots activism, public education, and the freedom to read. Laney resides in North Fort Worth with her husband and four children.

**Adam Bazaldua: Dallas City Councilman**

Deputy Mayor Pro Tem Bazaldua is the youngest elected Council Member to the City of Dallas in its current form of government.Bazaldua is a dedicated father and husband who has been a chef and a teacher. For the last five years, Council Member Adam Bazaldua has served as the City Council Member for Dallas' City Council District 7.

description:

The next meeting is **June 2nd**. When it's shared, the agenda will be available [here](https://www.franklincountync.gov/government/board_of_county_commissioners/agenda_minutes.php).

They meet in Franklin Plaza Training Room​ at 279 South Bickett Boulevard​, Louisburg, NC 27549​. This is the same place we had our county convention and the same building as the senior center. It's located next to Tractor Supply in the Food Lion shopping center.


**_Message shared on Commissioner Mark Speed's Facebook page:_**

Y’all, I want to speak plain for a minute.
On June 2 at 7pm, the Board of Commissioners is holding a public hearing—and I need folks from every corner of Franklin County to show up and speak up.

If you’ve got something on your heart about how your tax dollars are being spent—whether it’s roads, schools, public safety, recreation or any other budget item—this is your time to be heard.

title: Pasco Resists-Honor Veterans on D-Day

location.venue: Intersection of Little Rd and Citizens Dr

description:
On D-Day Anniversary, Pasco Resists Honors Veterans and Demands Protection of the VA

New Port Richey, FL — On the 81st anniversary of D-Day, Pasco Resists honors the sacrifice, bravery, and patriotism of American service members who fought on the beaches of Normandy to defend democracy and defeat fascism. A protest will take place on Friday June 6th from 4-6pm at the West Government Pasco Center, the intersection of Little Rd and Citizens Dr, (8731 Citizens Dr.)

“June 6 is a sacred date in our shared history,” said Doris Carroll, advocate, and leader with Pasco Resists. “It marks the moment when ordinary Americans did something extraordinary —risking everything to protect freedom not just for our nation, but for the world.”

The D-Day anniversary comes at a time when veterans face new battles at home. From underfunded healthcare to attempts to privatize and dismantle the VA, many veterans struggle to get the support they deserve after their service.

“Honoring our veterans means more than speeches—it means action,” said Carroll. “It means protecting the VA, expanding mental health care, and making sure no veteran is left behind.”

Pasco Resists is calling on elected officials and the public to recommit policies that truly honor the legacy of those who served. That includes rejecting VA budget cuts, improving access to healthcare, housing, and job opportunities, and standing against extremism in all forms.

“The men and women of D-Day didn’t fight to see their legacy used as a political prop,” Carroll added. “They fought for freedom, for equality, and for a better future. That’s the legacy we must live up to.”
________________________________________
About Pasco Resists
Pasco Resists is a grassroots organization based in Pasco County, Florida. We are dedicated to defending and uplifting veterans and working families through advocacy, education, and direct action. We believe a just society is one where every veteran receives the care, respect, and support they have earned.
